title: Pharmacogenomic Testing for Warfarin Response
service: Pharmacogenomic testing of CYP2C9 or VKORC1 alleles to predict warfarin response

criteria.text: Candidate for anticoagulation therapy with warfarin
criteria.span: covered only when provided to Medicare beneficiaries who are candidates for anticoagulation therapy with warfarin

criteria.text: Not previously tested for CYP2C9 or VKORC1 alleles
criteria.span: Have not been previously tested for CYP2C9 or VKORC1 alleles

criteria.text: Fewer than five days of warfarin in the regimen for which testing is ordered
criteria.span: Have received fewer than five days of warfarin in the anticoagulation regimen for which the testing is ordered

criteria.text: Enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled clinical study meeting the CED standards
criteria.span: Are enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled clinical study when that study meets the following standards.

criteria.text: Study registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before first subject enrolled
criteria.span: The clinical research study is registered on the www.ClinicalTrials.gov website by the principal sponsor/investigator prior to the enrollment of the first study subject.

criteria.text: Study has a written protocol addressing the Medicare standards
criteria.span: The research study has a written protocol that clearly addresses, or incorporates by reference, the Medicare standards.

pharmacogenomic testing of CYP2C9 or VKORC1 alleles to predict warfarin responsiveness improves health outcomes in Medicare beneficiaries outside the context of CED, and is therefore not reasonable and necessary

notes: Coverage is CED only. 'Fewer than five days of warfarin' counts days in the current regimen only; warfarin taken in an earlier, separate regimen does not count. Cases avoid other alleles and non-warfarin purposes, which the NCD expressly does not address (section C).
